title: Rava son of Rav Ada
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He and Ravin son of Rav Ada (possibly his brother, in Hyman’s conjecture) were students of Rav Yehudah, as in [Beitzah 33b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.33b.6), where they said, “When we were at Rav Yehudah’s.”

Both spoke in Rav Yehudah’s name, as in [Taanit 24b:12-13](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.24b.12-13) and [Ketubot 7b:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.7b.9). Hyman also has them speak in Rabbah’s name in [Yoma 53b:6-7](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.53b.6-7).[^2]

In [Kiddushin 70a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.70a.8), Rabbah son of Rav Ada speaks in the name of Rav. In [Menachot 39a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.39a.3), he cites Rav Ada in the name of Rav. Hyman suggests that possibly in Yoma and Kiddushin too the words “Rav Ada” are missing in the middle. For Makkot 18a (see [Makkot 18b:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Makkot.18b.15) in the consulted edition), Hyman cites Rava bar Ada speaking in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak; in [Sukkah 3a:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.3a.1): “Rabbah son of Rav Ada said: It is needed only,” etc.
Hyman reports that in the Venice printing it was written רב׳, and from this came Rabbah; but in fact his name was Rava.

notes.text: Possible brotherhood and the omitted Rav Ada are Hyman’s conjectures. His Venice-apostrophe explanation is reported, not new printed-pixel or correction-history evidence.

Taanit gives Ravin and Rava bar Ada in Rav Yehudah’s name. Ketubot reads Rabbah with Ravin, likewise in Rav Yehudah’s name. Yoma gives Rava and Ravin in Rav’s name, while the next passage has Rav Acha son of Rava cite Rav Yehudah. Hyman’s Rabbah reading and his suggested missing Rav Ada are his account.
